body_en: Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’
Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

“China urges the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” the Chinese commerce ministry spokesman, He Yadong, said at a regular briefing. “China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.”
Brazil was also singled out in the announcement after trade talks stalled.

Brazil’s government said on Wednesday that “Brazil will not yield to this type of threat”, adding in its statement that the “unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the framework of the ongoing bilateral negotiating process”.
A Democratic-controlled Congress will seek to constrain Trump’s foreign adventures
It voiced particular indignation at US proposals for higher import taxes for raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft, a change that would hit Embraer, Brazil’s largest aircraft maker.

It added that Brazil would continue to negotiate “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products”.

The Trump administration said that the new tariffs would be consistent with trade deals that the US reached last year with dozens of countries. They are being imposed under a law that allowed the president to target countries the US had found to engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, told CNBC that many US trading partners had adopted “market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base”.
The Trump administration’s new tariff rates would be capped at lower ​levels ‌agreed under ​trade deals ​that have already been concluded or remain under negotiation.
The administration will seek feedback from affected industries and hold a hearing on 25 January, suggesting the final duties won’t take effect until February or March.
Trump met his counterpart, Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen last week but the escalation in tariffs will not be a surprise to China, Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group’s China team, told AFP news agency.
The US and China last year reached a trade truce but that is set to expire on 10 January 2027. Trump and Xi are expected to meet again in Miami on the sidelines of the G20 in December.
“It has become a pattern before every major top leader summit,” Wang said, adding that she did not think the new measures would derail relations between Washington and Beijing.
“Xi has a high incentive to keep bilateral relations stable leading up to the 21st (Communist) party congress in October 2027,”Wang said.
A spokesperson for China’s embassy in Washington rejected allegations that China was ‌a source of ⁠excess capacity.

“The so-called issue of ‘industrial overcapacity’ does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation,” the spokesperson said, urging the two sides to jointly deliver on agreements secured between Trump andd Xi .
body_zh: 北京称新征税相当于“政治操纵”，而巴西“不会屈服于此类威胁”
特朗普提议对中国、欧盟等14个伙伴加征新关税
在唐纳德·特朗普政府提议对中国和其他主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税，引发全球强烈反对后，北京表示保留采取“必要措施”的权利。
在周三宣布的对 14 个主要贸易伙伴的建议征税计划中，中国可能是受到打击最大的国家之一。它将面临 20% 的最高税率，在某些情况下，该税率将与其他进口税叠加，总税率为 45%。
中国商务部发言人何亚东在例行记者会上表示，“中方敦促美方纠正错误做法，回到通过对话协商解决问题的正确轨道”。 “中方将密切关注事态发展，并保留采取必要措施的权利，坚决捍卫自身合法权益。”
在贸易谈判陷入僵局后，巴西也在声明中被单独点名。
巴西政府周三表示，“巴西不会屈服于此类威胁”，并在声明中补充说，“单方面决定在正在进行的双边谈判进程框架内构成不可接受的行动”。
民主党控制的国会将寻求限制特朗普的海外冒险
它对美国提出的提高原糖和精制糖进口税以及对飞机征收 10% 新关税的提议表示特别愤慨，这一变化将对巴西最大的飞机制造商巴西航空工业公司造成打击。
它补充说，巴西将继续进行谈判，“不排除采取报复措施以应对对巴西产品非法和不公正征收关税的可能性”。
特朗普政府表示，新关税将与美国去年与数十个国家达成的贸易协议保持一致。这些措施是根据一项法律实施的，该法律允许总统针对美国发现从事不合理或歧视性贸易行为的国家。美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 告诉 CNBC，许多美国贸易伙伴采取了“扭曲市场的做法，使贸易平衡向有利于他们的方向倾斜，同时侵蚀美国的制造业基础”。
特朗普政府的新关税税率将限制在已达成或仍在谈判中的贸易协议下商定的较低水平。
政府将寻求受影响行业的反馈，并于 1 月 25 日举行听证会，表明最终关税要到 2 月或 3 月才会生效。
欧亚集团中国团队总监王丹告诉法新社，特朗普上周在深圳会见了习近平，但关税升级不会令中国感到意外。
美国和中国去年达成了贸易休战，但该休战将于 2027 年 1 月 10 日到期。特朗普和习近平预计将于 12 月 G20 峰会期间在迈阿密再次会面。
王说：“这已成为每次主要领导人峰会之前的一种模式。”她补充说，她认为新措施不会破坏华盛顿和北京之间的关系。
王说：“习近平非常有动力在 2027 年 10 月召开第 21 次党代表大会之前保持双边关系稳定。”
中国驻华盛顿大使馆发言人否认了有关中国是产能过剩来源的指控，但没有威胁进行报复。
发言人表示：“所谓‘工业产能过剩’问题并不存在，不应成为政治操纵的借口。”他敦促双方共同落实唐纳德·特朗普和中国领导人习近平达成的协议。

summary_zh: 他的离开结束了一场关于正当程序和驱逐出境的备受瞩目的法律斗争，但特朗普政府几乎不需要承担任何责任
body_en: His departure ends a high-profile legal battle over due process and deportation, but leaves the Trump administration facing little accountability for its actions

Kilmar Ábrego García , the man illegally deported to his native El Salvador last year and whose immigration case spurred a 20-month-long battle with the Trump administration, arrived in Spain on Wednesday.
Trump administration officials and Ábrego García supporters are both claiming voluntary departure from the US to avoid deportation is a victory for their respective sides.
And they’re both sort of right, if such an ugly immigration spectacle can even be associated with concepts of victory.

On the one hand, Ábrego García has the relief of leaving the country seemingly his own accord, given that he was not going to be allowed to remain legally in the US. By going to Spain he avoids the pitfalls he had been facing. These were: being indefinitely detained inside a horrific prison in El Salvador, being sent to an unfamiliar African country where, if some other examples are anything to go by, he could end up in a prison or detained under harsh conditions in a secured hotel, indefinitely, or detained indefinitely in a US cell. His attorneys hope that, under a different president in the future, he may be allowed to return to the US.
And on the other hand, the Trump administration has won by getting rid of a high-profile immigrant they were determined not to let rest.

Ábrego García first arrived in the spotlight in March 2025, after the Trump administration deported him to El Salvador despite a US court order protecting him from being deported there , for his own safety. His case led to a nearly two-year-long “David and Goliath” type battle between him and the Trump administration, raising concerns about due process and constitutional rights, the separation of powers and accountability, the US government’s deals with countries for deportations and questionable federal prosecutions.

The entire case transcends the complicated character of Ábrego García himself. It has shown the world the lengths the Trump administration will go to when carrying out its anti-immigrant crackdown, and was an early example of the emboldened returning president defying federal court orders, to say nothing of fairness.

Ábrego García arrived in the US in 2011 from El Salvador without proper authorization and lived in Maryland for years, regularly checking in with Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ). He married a US citizen and had a child with her.

In 2019, he was arrested outside a hardware store in Maryland after local police, relying on an informant and what his lawyers called “ no evidence ”, accused him of being a gang member. He was turned over to ICE, but a judge ruled he should not be deported to his country of origin due to danger in that country. He continued with his life with a valid work permit.

Then in March 2025, ICE officials arrested him while driving home with his five-year-old son. And after the Trump administration had struck a deal with the Salvadorian government, run by the rightwing and self-proclaimed “world’s coolest dictator”, Nayib Bukele, ICE quickly deported Ábrego García to El Salvador along with dozens of Venezuelan men in one of the most infamous immigration actions of the second Trump administration. As the flights were midair, a federal judge ordered the Trump administration to turn them back , due to accusations of due process violations. The administration defied the federal judge. The men arrived in El Salvador and were violently taken to a notorious anti-terrorism prison called Cecot, ostensibly to be detained indefinitely. Many claimed they were tortured, assaulted, raped and traumatized by the ordeal.

In court filings, the Trump administration admitted they had mistakenly deported Ábrego García due to an “administrative error”. After a lengthy legal battle, including input from the US supreme court , the administration was ordered to return him to the US. They initially refused , but eventually he was brought back in June 2025.

The Trump administration then quickly charged him with crimes relating to human smuggling, based on a traffic stop in Tennessee dating from 2022, and he was detained again . In parallel with the criminal case, this allowed ICE to begin attempts to remove him to a series of African countries . Ábrego García and his legal team resisted. Then, presumably concluding he had no future as a free man in the US, he offered to be removed to Costa Rica. The administration refused to send him to the Central American country and pushed to deport him to Africa.

The government denigrated him publicly as a “gang member”, “human trafficker”, “wife beater” and “child predator”. They pointed to accusations that he had allegedly abused his wife. He had never committed any of those crimes.
However, his human smuggling case was dismissed in May of this year, with the federal judge saying it was a “vindictive prosecution”.

Negotiations continued behind closed doors. A court order unsealed on Wednesday shows that the federal judge presiding over his case had ordered the Trump administration to effectuate Ábrego García’s voluntary departure from the US. The judge ordered the administration not to intervene in his departure. On Tuesday, it was announced he was leaving the US voluntarily, but to Europe, not Central America. He duly arrived in Spain’s capital, Madrid, on Wednesday morning with his wife. Competing claims of victory broke out from Ábrego García’s supporters and the Trump administration.

“I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this administration’s constant persecution,” said Senator Chris Van Hollen, who visited Ábrego García in El Salvador and pushed for his return.

“We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Ábrego García has self-deported from the United States to Spain,” said homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin, using a favored Trump administration phrase when people leave the country specifically to avoid deportation.

The years-long and tired narrative of the “good” immigrant versus “bad” immigrant has only helped immigration hardliners justify the propping up of an aggressive enforcement system that targets all and tramples on due process rights, regardless of criminal history.
body_zh: 他的离开结束了一场关于正当程序和驱逐出境的备受瞩目的法律斗争，但特朗普政府几乎不需要对其行为承担责任
基尔马·阿夫雷戈·加西亚 (Kilmar Ábrego García) 于周三抵达西班牙，这名男子去年被非法驱逐回祖国萨尔瓦多，他的移民案引发了与特朗普政府长达 20 个月的斗争。
特朗普政府官员和阿夫雷戈·加西亚的支持者都声称自愿离开美国以避免被驱逐出境是双方的胜利。
如果如此丑陋的移民景象甚至可以与胜利的概念联系起来，他们都是对的。
一方面，鉴于阿夫雷戈·加西亚不会被允许在美国合法居留，他似乎自愿离开美国，这让他松了口气。通过前往西班牙，他避免了一直面临的陷阱。这些是：被无限期地关押在萨尔瓦多的一个可怕的监狱里，被送到一个陌生的非洲国家，如果有其他一些例子的话，他最终可能会被关进监狱，或者被无限期地关押在条件恶劣的安全酒店里，或者被无限期地关押在美国的牢房里。他的律师希望，在未来另一位总统的领导下，他可能会被允许返回美国。
另一方面，特朗普政府通过摆脱他们决心不让的高调移民而赢得了胜利。
2025 年 3 月，阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 首次成为人们关注的焦点，当时特朗普政府将他驱逐到萨尔瓦多，尽管美国法院出于自身安全考虑，下令保护他不被驱逐到萨尔瓦多。他的案件导致他与特朗普政府之间进行了近两年的“以弱胜强”式的斗争，引发了人们对正当程序和宪法权利、权力分立和问责制、美国政府与各国的驱逐协议以及可疑的联邦起诉的担忧。
整个案件超越了阿布雷戈·加西亚本人的复杂性格。它向世界展示了特朗普政府在进行反移民镇压时将采取的措施，也是这位重返总统大胆无视联邦法院命令的早期例子，更不用说公平了。
阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 于 2011 年在未经适当授权的情况下从萨尔瓦多抵达美国，并在马里兰州生活了多年，定期接受移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 的检查。他与一位美国公民结婚并与她育有一个孩子。
2019年，他在马里兰州一家五金店外被捕，当地警方依靠线人以及他的律师所谓的“没有证据”指控他是帮派成员。他被移交给 ICE，但法官裁定，由于该国存在危险，不应将他驱逐回原籍国。他持有有效的工作许可证继续他的生活。

然后在 2025 年 3 月，ICE 官员在他带着五岁儿子开车回家时逮捕了他。在特朗普政府与自称“世界上最酷的独裁者”的右翼人士纳伊布·布克莱 (Nayib Bukele) 领导的萨尔瓦多政府达成协议后，ICE 迅速将阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 和数十名委内瑞拉男子驱逐到萨尔瓦多，这是特朗普第二届政府中最臭名昭著的移民行动之一。由于航班在半空中，一名联邦法官以违反正当程序为由，命令特朗普政府将其返航。政府藐视联邦法官。这些人抵达萨尔瓦多，并被暴力带到臭名昭著的名为塞科特的反恐监狱，表面上是无限期拘留。许多人声称他们受到酷刑、殴打、强奸和精神创伤。
在法庭文件中，特朗普政府承认，由于“行政错误”，他们错误地驱逐了阿布雷戈·加西亚。经过漫长的法律斗争，包括美国最高法院的意见，政府被命令将他遣返回美国。他们最初拒绝了，但最终于 2025 年 6 月将他带回来。
特朗普政府随后以2022年田纳西州的一次交通截查为由，迅速指控他犯有与人口走私有关的罪行，他再次被拘留。在刑事案件的同时，ICE 开始尝试将他移送至一系列非洲国家。阿布雷戈·加西亚和他的法律团队进行了抵制。然后，他大概认为自己在美国作为自由人没有未来，于是主动提出被遣送至哥斯达黎加。政府拒绝将他送往中美洲国家，并极力将他驱逐到非洲。
政府公开诋毁他为“帮派成员”、“人贩子”、“殴打妻子”和“掠夺儿童的人”。他们指出了他涉嫌虐待妻子的指控。他从未犯过任何这些罪行。
然而，他的人口走私案于今年5月被驳回，联邦法官称这是“报复性起诉”。
闭门谈判仍在继续。周三公布的一份法院命令显示，主持该案的联邦法官已命令特朗普政府实现阿布雷戈·加西亚自愿离开美国。法官命令政府不要干预他的离境。周二，有消息称他将自愿离开美国，但前往欧洲，而不是中美洲。周三上午，他与妻子准时抵达西班牙首都马德里。阿布雷戈·加西亚的支持者和特朗普政府爆发了相互竞争的胜利声明。
“我感到欣慰的是，他将在他选择的国家安全、自由，包括免受本届政府持续的迫害，”参议员克里斯·范·霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)说，他访问了萨尔瓦多的阿布雷戈·加西亚并推动他回国。
“我们很高兴地宣布基尔马·阿夫雷戈·加西亚已从美国自行驱逐到西班牙，”国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林说，他使用了特朗普政府在人们专门为了避免被驱逐出境而离开美国时常用的短语。
多年来关于“好”移民与“坏”移民的陈词滥调，只会帮助移民强硬派证明支持针对所有人并践踏正当程序权利（无论犯罪历史如何）的激进执法体系是合理的。

title_en: Kilmar Ábrego García, target of Trump’s immigration crackdown, lands in Spain after ‘leaving happy’
title_zh: 特朗普移民镇压目标基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚在“快乐离开”后抵达西班牙
summary: Ábrego García chooses to depart from US after previously being deported to El Salvador due to ‘administrative error’ Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadorian national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts,
summary_zh: 阿尔布雷戈·加西亚（Ábrego García）因“行政错误”而被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，之后选择离开美国 Kilmar Ábrego García，萨尔瓦多
body_en: Ábrego García chooses to depart from US after previously being deported to El Salvador due to ‘administrative error’
Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadorian national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts, has landed in Spain.
Ábrego García arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States of his own volition .

“I feel free of everything evil that has followed me up until this point,” he told reporters on a video call just hours after he touched down. “I’m happy … because this time I’m leaving with my freedom, not like before when they took me out inhumanely.”
He added: “The government does not decide where my story continues. My family and I will decide our future.”
Prior to his departure, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents met him at the airport and removed his ankle monitor, according to We Are Casa, a Maryland-based advocacy group.
As he made his way through the Madrid airport, Ábrego García did not speak to reporters, instead raising his fist in the air as he climbed into a waiting van.
Ábrego García became a lightning rod in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in 2025 after he was deported to El Salvador in what an official later called an “administrative error”.

The 31-year-old had been living in the US since 2019, after a judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador due to the dangers posed by a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under ICE supervision, but he was not given residency status.

Married to an American woman, the Maryland resident was part of a group of more than 200 people sent by the US to Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison , in violation of the US immigration judge’s 2019 order.

Amid public outcry, he was returned to the US after a decision by the supreme court. Since then, Ábrego García has been fighting government efforts to deport him for a second time to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security officials.
On Wednesday, his lawyer, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, said the Trump administration had wanted to deport Ábrego García “handcuffed, on an ICE flight bound for Liberia” on Tuesday.

“And what happened? He walked out a free man, without any restrictions, without shackles on his feet. He left for the country of his choosing, and he did so on a commercial flight, alongside everyone else,” Sandoval-Moshenberg added.
He described it as a “complete victory”, adding: “Instead of flying ICE Air, he flew United Airlines. Instead of being in shackles, he was in economy plus.”

He said Ábrego García had negotiated a deal with federal authorities in which they had agreed to allow him to leave the country, removing obstacles such as the ankle monitor and taking him off the no-fly list, as long as he left by 24 November. The Department of Homeland Security said on Tuesday Ábrego García had “self-deported” to Spain .

Sandoval-Moshenberg described Ábrego García’s departure from the US as temporary, saying that he would decide where to settle for the next two years as he waited out the remainder of the Trump administration.

“Mr Ábrego García has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a US citizen spouse and the father of a US citizen child,” he said. “We don’t expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritise reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland.”

On Wednesday, Ábrego García’s lawyer, Chris Newman, said his client had landed in Spain as a tourist and that he had no plans to meet with any politicians while in Spain. “I can confirm that he’s coming here with the intention of staying for just a few days and that he already has tickets, one could say, for his next appointment,” he told Spanish media.
His departure this week was celebrated by many who had sought to push back against the Trump administration’s pursuit of Ábrego García.
body_zh: 阿布雷戈·加西亚（Ábrego García）因“行政错误”被驱逐到萨尔瓦多后选择离开美国
萨尔瓦多国民基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Kilmar Ábrego García) 已抵达西班牙，他的错误驱逐使他成为唐纳德·特朗普大规模驱逐行动的象征。
阿布雷戈·加西亚在自愿离开美国后于周三抵达马德里。
“我感觉自己已经摆脱了迄今为止一直伴随着我的一切邪恶，”他在着陆几小时后在视频通话中对记者说。 “我很高兴……因为这次我带着自由离开，而不是像以前那样不人道地把我带走。”
他补充道：“政府不能决定我的故事在哪里继续。我和我的家人将决定我们的未来。”
据马里兰州倡导组织 We Are Casa 称，在他出发之前，移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 特工在机场迎接了他，并取下了他的脚踝监视器。
当阿布雷戈·加西亚穿过马德里机场时，他没有对记者讲话，而是在爬上一辆等候的面包车时举起拳头。
阿夫雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，后来一名官员称这是“行政错误”，他因此成为特朗普政府 2025 年移民镇压的避雷针。
这位 31 岁的男子自 2019 年以来一直居住在美国，此前一名法官裁定，由于一个威胁他家人的团伙构成的危险，他不能被驱逐到萨尔瓦多。法官允许他在 ICE 的监督下在美国生活和工作，但没有给予他居留身份。
这位马里兰州居民与一名美国妇女结婚，是美国违反美国移民法官 2019 年的命令，将 200 多人送往臭名昭著的反恐巨型监狱塞科特 (Cecot) 的一员之一。
在公众的强烈抗议下，最高法院做出裁决后，他被遣返美国。从那时起，阿布雷戈·加西亚一直在反对政府根据国土安全部官员的提议第二次将他驱逐到一系列非洲国家的努力。
周三，他的律师西蒙·桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格 (Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg) 表示，特朗普政府希望周二将阿布雷戈·加西亚“戴上手铐，乘坐飞往利比里亚的 ICE 航班”驱逐出境。
“发生了什么事？他以自由人的身份走出去，没有任何限制，脚上没有镣铐。他前往他选择的国家，并与其他人一起乘坐商业航班，”桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格补充道。
他形容这是一次“彻底的胜利”，并补充道：“他没有乘坐ICE航空，而是乘坐联合航空。他没有受到束缚，而是乘坐了经济舱。”
他说，阿布雷戈·加西亚已与联邦当局谈判达成一项协议，同意允许他离开该国，取消脚踝监视器等障碍，并将他从禁飞名单上删除，只要他在 11 月 24 日之前离开即可。美国国土安全部周二表示，阿布雷戈·加西亚已“自行驱逐”至西班牙。
桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格称阿布雷戈·加西亚离开美国是暂时的，并表示他将在等待特朗普政府剩余任期的同时决定未来两年的定居地点。
“作为美国公民配偶的丈夫和美国公民孩子的父亲，阿布雷戈·加西亚先生有多种选择返回美国，”他说。 “我们预计这不会在本届政府领导下发生，我们知道这永远不会给他带来公平的待遇，但我们预计下一届政府将优先考虑让这个家庭团聚并将他带回马里兰州。”
周三，阿布雷戈·加西亚的律师克里斯·纽曼表示，他的当事人以游客身份抵达西班牙，他没有计划在西班牙期间会见任何政客。他告诉西班牙媒体：“我可以证实，他来这里只是打算待几天，而且他已经有了下一次约会的门票。”
许多曾试图阻止特朗普政府追捕阿夫雷戈·加西亚的人本周庆祝了他的离职。

title_en: Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU
title_zh: 特朗普提议对中国、欧盟等14个伙伴加征新关税
summary: Administration is suggesting an added 20% tax on Chinese imports, which would bring the total to about 40% US politics live – latest updates Donald Trump is proposing new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the European Union, that would go int
summary_zh: 政府建议对中国进口商品加征 20% 的关税，这将使美国政坛的关税总额达到约 40%——唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Tr) 最新动态
body_en: Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU | Trump tariffs
Administration is suggesting an added 20% tax on Chinese imports, which would bring the total to about 40%

Donald Trump is proposing new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the European Union, that would go into effect early next year, the office of the US trade representative said on Wednesday.

The administration is proposing an additional 20% tax on Chinese imports, which would bring the total tax to about 40%. Other countries and regions affected by the new tariffs include Bangladesh, ‌Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

In February, the supreme court ruled Trump’s so-called Liberation Day tariffs illegal. The court issued a narrow decision saying the administration had improperly used a specific emergency powers law to implement the tariffs, but did not broadly curb the president’s power to introduce new tariffs.

The administration is now using section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 as the legal basis for the new rounds of tariffs. The law gives the executive branch power to respond to unfair foreign trade practices after conducting formal investigations.

Though the White House did not give a timeline for the new tariffs, it said they could go into effect in January at the earliest. The US trade office said it would hold hearings on the new tariffs and its investigation into the unfair trade practices on 25 January.

This is the second major batch of section 301 tariffs, after the White House announced a broad slate of tariffs on more than 80 countries in July, including the UK, Mexico and Canada, saying the countries had failed to enforce bans on forced labor. A lawsuit fighting those tariffs is currently awaiting a decision in the court of international trade.

“For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America’s manufacturing base,” the US trade representative, Jamieson Greer, said in a statement on Wednesday.

“President Trump is proposing to take action to bring about the elimination of these unfair acts, policies, and practices. In doing so, we can level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.”

Tariffs have proven unpopular with US voters, who handed Democrats a decisive victory in the midterm elections that will give the party control of Congress. The Yale Budget Lab estimates that tariffs currently in effect have added an additional $900 annually in costs for each US household.

The rising cost of living was the number one issue for voters ahead of November’s midterm elections, according to a Harris Poll survey for the Guardian. An earlier Harris poll found seven in 10 Americans blamed tariffs for higher prices.
Consumer prices rose an annualized 3.8% in October, the Bureau of Economic Analysis announced on Wednesday, the highest rate since May and well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% annual target.
body_zh: 特朗普提议对中国、欧盟等14个合作伙伴征收新关税特朗普关税
政府建议对中国进口商品加征 20% 的关税，这将使关税总额达到 40% 左右
美国贸易代表办公室周三表示，唐纳德·特朗普提议对包括中国和欧盟在内的 14 个贸易伙伴征收新关税，该关税将于明年初生效。
政府提议对中国进口产品额外征收 20% 的税，这将使总税收达到 40% 左右。其他受新关税影响的国家和地区包括孟加拉国、柬埔寨、欧盟、印度、印度尼西亚、日本、韩国、马来西亚、新加坡、瑞士、台湾、泰国和越南。
今年二月，最高法院裁定特朗普所谓的解放日关税非法。法院发布了一项狭隘的裁决，称政府不恰当地使用特定的紧急权力法来实施关税，但没有广泛限制总统征收新关税的权力。
政府目前正在使用 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条作为新一轮关税的法律依据。该法律赋予行政部门在进行正式调查后对不公平外贸行为做出反应的权力。
尽管白宫没有给出新关税的时间表，但表示最早可能在一月份生效。美国贸易办公室表示，将于 1 月 25 日就新关税和不公平贸易行为调查举行听证会。
这是继 7 月份白宫宣布对包括英国、墨西哥和加拿大在内的 80 多个国家征收广泛关税后，第二批 301 关税措施，称这些国家未能执行强迫劳动禁令。目前，针对这些关税的诉讼正在等待国际贸易法院的裁决。
美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)周三在一份声明中表示：“几十年来，我们的许多贸易伙伴采取了针对制造业、工资和劳动力抑制、金融和其他支持、非市场经济投入以及其他市场扭曲做法的产业战略，这些做法使贸易平衡向有利于他们的方向倾斜，同时侵蚀了美国的制造业基础。”
“特朗普总统提议采取行动消除这些不公平的行为、政策和做法。通过这样做，我们可以为美国工人创造公平的竞争环境，并为世界经济制定一条新的、更可持续的路线。”
事实证明，关税不受美国选民欢迎，民主党在中期选举中取得了决定性胜利，从而使该党控制了国会。耶鲁大学预算实验室估计，目前生效的关税每年会给每个美国家庭额外增加 900 美元的成本。
根据《卫报》的哈里斯民意调查，生活成本上涨是十一月中期选举前选民面临的首要问题。哈里斯早些时候的一项民意调查发现，十分之七的美国人将价格上涨归咎于关税。
美国经济分析局周三宣布，10 月份消费者价格年率上涨 3.8%，为 5 月份以来的最高涨幅，远高于美联储 2% 的年度目标。

title_en: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
title_zh: 美国法官裁定 FCC 侵犯 ABC 的言论自由权以取悦特朗普
summary: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查美国广播公司持有的所有当地广播许可证。该电台在其中六个地区播出
body_en: U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump : NPR

U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.

Under Chairman Brendan Carr, left, the Federal Communications Commission launched an early review of Disney's licenses to operate all the local ABC stations it owns. New Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro, right, says the company is fighting back to protect ABC's journalistic integrity and free speech. "We're very principled on this," he said. Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment for satire, commentary and news coverage that Trump doesn't like.
Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections

In her preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan found that the federal agency's early reviews represented retaliation for speech the Trump administration resented.

Such perceived offenses included late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's jabs at the president, the critical remarks of hosts on the chat show The View , and the moderation of a presidential debate in September 2024.

ABC and its corporate parent, the Walt Disney Co., serve six of the 10 largest markets in the U.S., including New York, Los Angeles, and Houston. They contribute significantly to the network's bottom line.

"Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face -- loss of their broadcast licenses -- the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," Judge AliKhan wrote.

She rejected the Trump administration's motion to dismiss the lawsuit from ABC and Disney challenging the review of the local licenses. Usually the licenses last eight years and are up for review on a staggered basis. They are rarely taken away.

In her ruling, AliKhan relied heavily on public statements and social media postings in which Trump attacked ABC and Disney, as well as posts by Trump's pick as the chair of the Federal Communications Commission, Brendan Carr.

"What started in 2020 as questions about how ABC 'can keep getting a license' if it 'report[s] fake news,' ... has crescendoed into repeated calls for the Commission to strip ABC's broadcast licenses for their editorial decisions," she wrote. "The court counts eleven such calls made by President Trump over the past two years -- the most recent being in July 2026."
And the judge cited the administration's "tangible steps toward enforcing President Trump and Commissioner Carr's repeated threats to strip the Plaintiff Stations of their licenses."
"Chairman Carr has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders," Judge AliKhan wrote.
Carr did not respond to NPR's request for comment Wednesday evening.
ABC hailed the ruling in a statement as "an important victory for the First Amendment."

Among the targets of ire from Trump and Carr was ABC's decision not to broadcast Trump's July 2026 Oval Office address on its television network. ABC's legal team said the network streamed it on its digital news service, but would not have done so absent the political pressure from the FCC.

It is one of several examples of newsroom decisions made under duress, the network's lawyers said in court. Kimmel's interview with then-Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico of Texas was uploaded to YouTube instead of being aired on ABC's late night television show. (Talarico won election to the U.S. Senate earlier this month.) And The View stopped hosting candidates for political office in 2026 in the months ahead of the fall elections.
body_zh: 美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯了ABC的言论自由 : NPR
美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯ABC的言论自由 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查ABC持有的所有当地广播许可证。这些电台在美国六个最大的市场播出。
在主席布伦丹·卡尔（左）的领导下，联邦通信委员会对迪士尼拥有的所有当地 ABC 电视台的运营许可证进行了早期审查。迪士尼新任首席执行官乔什·达马罗（右）表示，公司正在反击，以保护 ABC 的新闻诚信和言论自由。 “我们对此非常有原则，”他说。 Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/法新社来自 Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
一名联邦法官阻止特朗普总统及其政府采取行动挑战美国广播公司电视网络的广播许可证，认为这是对特朗普不喜欢的讽刺、评论和新闻报道的违宪惩罚。
迪士尼和美国广播公司 (ABC) 在法庭上就言论自由保护问题与特朗普的联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 展开斗争
美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗在周三提交的初步禁令中发现，联邦机构的早期审查是对特朗普政府不满的言论的报复。
此类被视为冒犯的行为包括深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔对总统的攻击、主持人在脱口秀节目《The View》中的批评言论，以及对 2024 年 9 月总统辩论的缓和。
ABC 及其母公司华特迪士尼公司为美国 10 个最大市场中的 6 个提供服务，包括纽约、洛杉矶和休斯顿。它们对网络的盈利做出了重大贡献。
法官写道：“鉴于原告可能面临的惩罚的极端性，甚至是生死攸关的性质——失去广播许可证——法院的结论是，过早的许可证续签程序所造成的风险足以让一家普通的广播公司感到不寒而栗。”
她拒绝了特朗普政府驳回美国广播公司和迪士尼对当地许可审查提出质疑的诉讼的动议。通常，许可证的有效期为八年，并且会分阶段接受审查。他们很少被带走。
阿里汗在裁决中严重依赖特朗普攻击美国广播公司和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及特朗普任命的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的帖子。
她写道：“从 2020 年开始，人们开始质疑 ABC 如果‘报道假新闻’，如何‘能够继续获得许可证’……现在已经逐渐演变成一再呼吁委员会取消 ABC 因其编辑决定而获得的广播许可证。” “法院统计特朗普总统在过去两年中发出了 11 次此类电话——最近一次是在 2026 年 7 月。”
法官还援引了政府“为执行特朗普总统和卡尔专员一再威胁吊销原告电视台执照而采取的切实步骤”。
阿里汗法官写道：“卡尔主席已将特朗普总统的言论作为他的行军命令。”
周三晚上，卡尔没有回应 NPR 的置评请求。
美国广播公司在一份声明中称赞这一裁决是“第一修正案的重要胜利”。
特朗普和卡尔愤怒的目标之一是美国广播公司 (ABC) 决定不在其电视网络上播出特朗普 2026 年 7 月在椭圆形办公室的讲话。美国广播公司的法律团队表示，该网络在其数字新闻服务上播放了该节目，但如果没有联邦通信委员会的政治压力，美国广播公司不会这样做。
该网络的律师在法庭上表示，这是新闻编辑室在胁迫下做出决定的几个例子之一。基梅尔对当时的美国民主党参议员候选人、来自德克萨斯州的詹姆斯·塔拉里科的采访被上传到 YouTube，而不是在美国广播公司的深夜电视节目中播出。 （塔拉里科本月早些时候赢得了美国参议院选举。）在秋季选举前的几个月，The View 停止接待 2026 年政治职务候选人。

body_en: Senator-elect Troy Jackson , of Maine, has endorsed Chris Van Hollen for Senate majority leader, a blow to the current minority leader, Chuck Schumer , ahead of a vote among Senate Democrats next Tuesday.

The Maryland senator has successfully cast himself as a “change” candidate following Democrats’ sweeping success in the midterms, whereas Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for the last decade, is seen as the “establishment” figure in the race, representing the status quo.

Van Hollen and the argument for a new generation of leadership has received backing from Bernie Sanders , incoming senators Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan and others, as well as some celebrity backing from the likes of Robert De Niro , Jane Fonda , and others.

“I’ve talked with Mainers about what they need from the Senate, and I believe it’s time for a change in leadership. I’ll be voting for Senator Van Hollen ,” Jackson said in a statement. “When we spoke, I told him Maine needs a seat at the table when the caucus decides what gets funded and what we’re going to fight for. I was impressed by his vision for the caucus, and I came away confident he’ll take Maine’s priorities seriously .

“From one end of Maine to the other, I heard the same thing. People are working harder, falling further behind, and getting tired of being told to wait. Senator Van Hollen and I agree that it’s time to end the filibuster, pass Medicare for All, and give working people a raise by increasing the minimum wage . I want a leader who’ll bring those fights to the floor and make every senator say where they stand.

“ Mainers voted for change in November, and they ought to get it. Whoever leads this caucus, I’ll fight like hell to make sure the Senate takes on the problems Mainers sent me to Washington to solve.”
body_zh: 缅因州当选参议员特洛伊·杰克逊（Troy Jackson）支持克里斯·范·霍伦（Chris Van Hollen）担任参议院多数党领袖，这对现任少数党领袖查克·舒默（Chuck Schumer）来说是一个打击，下周二参议院民主党将进行投票。
在民主党在中期选举中取得压倒性胜利后，这位马里兰州参议员成功地将自己塑造成“变革”候选人，而过去十年一直领导参议院民主党的舒默则被视为竞选中的“建制派”人物，代表着现状。
范霍伦和新一代领导层的主张得到了伯尼·桑德斯、即将上任的参议员阿卜杜勒·赛义德和佩吉·弗拉纳根等人的支持，以及罗伯特·德尼罗、简·方达等人的一些名人的支持。
“我已经与迈纳斯人讨论了他们需要参议院提供什么，我相信现在是改变领导层的时候了。我将投票给范霍伦参议员，”杰克逊在一份声明中说。 “当我们谈话时，我告诉他，当核心小组决定资助什么以及我们要争取什么时，缅因州需要在谈判桌上占有一席之地。他对核心小组的愿景给我留下了深刻的印象，我相信他会认真对待缅因州的优先事项。
“从缅因州的一端到另一端，我都听到了同样的事情。人们工作更加努力，落后得更多，并厌倦了被告知要等待。范霍伦参议员和我都同意，是时候结束阻挠议事，通过全民医疗保险，并通过提高最低工资来给工薪阶层加薪了。我想要一位领导人能够将这些斗争带到现场，让每位参议员表明自己的立场。
“迈纳斯在 11 月投票支持变革，他们应该得到它。无论谁领导这个核心小组，我都会拼命奋斗，以确保参议院解决迈纳斯派我去华盛顿解决的问题。”

body_en: Communities say big railroad companies won’t act and that lawmakers moving too slowly to address a major problem
The drive from the Lockland fire station to a house fire on Patterson Avenue should have taken no more than 45 seconds .

But East Wyoming Avenue and Davis Street were both blocked: a Norfolk Southern train was stopped across several streets – the fire engine had to turn around and take a detour via a nearby highway. By the time firefighters snaked through the highway traffic and reached the fire last month, seven minutes after the call came in, 89-year-old Marian Haefner was dead in her own home .
“We lost a house here about five years ago, on Central Avenue which is directly on the other side of the tracks. Same thing, couldn’t get to it,” says Mark Mason, Lockland’s mayor.
“I’ve been mayor of Lockland for nine years. Frankly, [Norfolk Southern] don’t give a crap. If they did, they would do something about it.”

From his office in a century-old building in Lockland, a small community north of Cincinnati, Mason reels off a list of complaints about train crossing blockages he’s been fielding: People threatened with dismissal because they are constantly late to work. Parents paying extra to daycares because they’re late picking up their children. College students who have had to drop out of a class because they can’t get to campus on time.

Lockland is several miles south of the Sharonville intermodal terminal, a link of the Heartland Corridor that links an Atlantic seaport in Norfolk, Virginia, with Chicago. It is from this terminal that Norfolk Southern trains are moved on to the tracks across Lockland streets, sometimes for up to 23 hours, to make room for other trains to be connected, say local officials.

“I’ve had it. It’s 2026 – trains should not be affecting people’s lives like this, much less putting them in danger. It’s an easy fix – quit pulling out trains if they can’t move forward [but train companies] are a powerful entity,” Mason says.
Rail companies own most tracks and lines in the US. Local and state authorities have scant ability to regulate.
Lockland is far from alone in dealing with Norfolk Southern, a $73bn public company with a long line of environmental and other charges against it.
Similar rail crossing incidents have been happening in Cleveland , Chicago , Houston and beyond.

In Hammond, Indiana a 2023 Pro Publica investigation found children regularly having to climb through cars to get to and from school. Local administrators say Norfolk Southern backed out of building a pedestrian overpass.

Over the past 12 months there have been more than 34,000 public reports of rail crossing blockages, according to the Federal Railroad Administration, a sharp increase from more than 25,000 reports over the previous 12 months. Texas alone made up almost 10,000 of those, with Ohio seeing the third-highest number of reports in that time.

In almost a quarter of those incidents, pedestrians crawling on, over or between rail cars were reported. In nearly 22%, first responders were unable to cross the tracks. Numerous other reports found students at the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa having to climb through stopped cars to get to campus.
In 2023, Houston reported 5,610 reports of blocked rail crossings, with the city’s East End reporting the highest number of complaints in the country, according to local reports.
Last December, Sylvia Garcia, a Texas congresswoman whose district includes the East End, reintroduced a bill prohibiting trains from blocking rail crossings for more than 10 minutes.

“We tragically lost 15-year-old Sergio Rodriguez , who was killed by an oncoming train while trying to get to Milby high school. No child should have to risk their life getting to school, and no family should have to worry about a blocked train delaying emergency care. Our communities deserve better,” she says.

“Republicans have allowed this legislation to languish in committee while powerful railroad companies continue putting their bottom lines ahead of the safety of our communities. These companies have spent years making promises while our families continue paying the price.”

Ohioans have had a troubled relationship with Norfolk Southern in recent years. In February 2023, a failed wheel bearing caused a train derailment and catastrophic chemical fire in East Palestine. The company settledwith the justice department and Environmental Protection Agency for more than $310m.
body_zh: 社区表示大型铁路公司不会采取行动，立法者在解决重大问题上行动太慢
从洛克兰消防局开车到帕特森大道发生火灾的房屋应该不会超过 45 秒。
但东怀俄明大道和戴维斯街均被封锁：一列诺福克南方火车在几条街道上被拦住，消防车不得不掉头绕道附近的高速公路。上个月，接到电话七分钟后，当消防队员蜿蜒穿过高速公路交通到达火场时，89 岁的玛丽安·海夫纳 (Marian Haefner) 已死在自己的家中。
“大约五年前，我们在中央大街失去了一栋房子，就在铁轨的另一边。同样的情况，我们无法到达，”洛克兰市长马克·梅森说。
“我担任洛克兰市市长已有九年了。坦率地说，[诺福克南方]根本不在乎。如果他们这么做，他们会采取一些措施。”
梅森在位于辛辛那提北部小社区洛克兰的一栋百年建筑内的办公室里，滔滔不绝地列出了他一直在处理的一系列有关火车道口堵塞的投诉：人们因为经常上班迟到而受到解雇威胁。父母因为接孩子迟到而向日托中心支付额外费用。由于无法按时到达校园而不得不退学的大学生。
洛克兰位于沙伦维尔联运码头以南几英里处，该码头是连接弗吉尼亚州诺福克大西洋海港和芝加哥的中心地带走廊的一环。当地官员表示，诺福克南方铁路的火车就是从这个终点站转移到洛克兰街道对面的铁轨上，有时长达 23 小时，以便为其他火车腾出空间。
“我已经受够了。现在是 2026 年了，火车不应该像这样影响人们的生活，更不用说让他们处于危险之中。解决办法很简单，如果火车无法前进，就不再拉动它们（但火车公司）是一个强大的实体，”梅森说。
铁路公司拥有美国大部分轨道和线路。地方和州当局缺乏监管能力。
洛克兰并不是唯一一家与诺福克南方公司打交道的公司，这家市值 730 亿美元的上市公司面临着一系列环境和其他指控。
类似的铁路交叉口事件在克利夫兰、芝加哥、休斯顿等地也发生过。
在印第安纳州哈蒙德，Pro Publica 2023 年的一项调查发现，孩子们经常需要爬汽车上下学。当地管理人员表示，诺福克南方铁路公司放弃了修建人行天桥的计划。
根据联邦铁路管理局的数据，过去 12 个月内，已有超过 34,000 份有关铁路道口堵塞的公开报告，较前 12 个月的 25,000 多份报告大幅增加。仅德克萨斯州就占了近 10,000 起，俄亥俄州的报告数量当时排名第三。
据报道，在这些事件中，近四分之一是行人在火车车厢上、上方或之间爬行。近 22% 的急救人员无法穿越铁轨。许多其他报告发现，塔斯卡卢萨阿拉巴马大学的学生必须爬过停着的汽车才能到达校园。
据当地报道，2023 年，休斯顿报告了 5,610 起铁路道口堵塞的报告，其中该市东区的投诉数量为全国最多。
去年12月，德克萨斯州女议员西尔维娅·加西亚（Sylvia Garcia）的选区包括东区，重新提出一项法案，禁止火车阻塞铁路道口超过10分钟。
“我们不幸失去了 15 岁的塞尔吉奥·罗德里格斯 (Sergio Rodriguez)，他在试图前往米尔比 (Milby) 高中时被迎面驶来的火车撞死。任何孩子都不应该冒着生命危险去上学，任何家庭也不应该担心火车受阻而延误紧急护理。我们的社区值得更好，”她说。
“共和党人允许这项立法在委员会中搁置，而强大的铁路公司继续将自己的底线置于我们社区的安全之上。这些公司花了数年时间做出承诺，而我们的家庭却继续付出代价。”
近年来，俄亥俄州与诺福克南方航空的关系一直存在问题。 2023 年 2 月，车轮轴承故障导致东巴勒斯坦发生火车脱轨和灾难性化学火灾。该公司与司法部和环境保护局达成和解，赔偿金额超过 3.1 亿美元。

Storm Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade, Trump's New Tariffs, Iowa Post-Detonation

Severe storms sweeping across the nation threaten to cause widespread travel delays today , as millions of people gather with their loved ones. New York City officials announced that the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been rescheduled to Saturday due to the threat of powerful wind gusts that could reach up to 60 mph. This year marked the 100th procession, and the first time the iconic event is being postponed.

Workers inflate the Spider-Man balloon during Macy's Balloon Inflation 2026 on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Macy's plans to celebrate its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade with a record 100 inflatables, but forecasted high winds are threatening to ground the giant balloons. Adam Gray/Getty Images hide caption

🎧 Something is happening across almost every part of the country right now , NPR's Kat Lonsdorf tells Up First . Extreme high tides are affecting the West Coast, snow is expected in parts of the Midwest, and in the South and Southeast, a major storm is advancing up the East Coast. Meteorologist Richard Bann with the National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center tells Lonsdorf the East Coast storm is the primary concern . Bann says the storm will become better organized throughout the day, bringing strong winds and heavy rain that could lead to coastal flooding. The good news: Forecasters expect the East Coast's major storm to move on, mostly wrapping up by Saturday, Lonsdorf says.

The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs targeting goods from 14 major U.S. trading partners , including China, Japan and the European Union. Administration officials argue the measures counter unfair foreign trade practices, though critics question their ultimate effectiveness. Proposed rates may reach 40% on Chinese imports, 35% on Vietnamese goods, and 20-25% on products from other targeted nations. Additional tariffs on Brazilian sugar and aircraft are also being suggested.

🎧 U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer said that new tariffs could take effect within a couple of months. For each country, the White House has listed a "proposed" rate and a "deal" rate, NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben says. For example, if talks with China progress positively, they may receive a deal rate of 20%, which is different from its proposed rate of 40%. Although the Supreme Court overturned President Trump's previous tariffs, the new ones fall under Section 301 , a law meant to counter unfair trade practices. The administration says these countries exhibit "structural excess capacity" in various manufactured goods, a situation caused by policies that lead to overproduction, which can distort the global market.

Federal scientists are testing the air, soil and water in Eastern Iowa for lead contamination after the U.S. Army detonated thousands of pounds of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown yesterday. Officials said the controlled explosion was the only safe way to dispose of the bomb-making compound.

🎧 Eliza Billingham of NPR network station Iowa Public Radio says the major concern is the potential release of lead into the air from the explosion. She adds that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has tested the area since the detonation and hasn't found lead in the air. The EPA has deployed around 300 people to sample the air, ground and nearby water. Lead is a neurotoxin that especially endangers children and pregnant people because it can impede childhood development. After a week and a half of delays and inconsistent communication from the Army, residents have grown hesitant about the Army and the EPA's initial findings, Billingham says. Residents want independent monitoring and the University of Iowa and the University of Illinois are conducting regional sampling. Results are expected in a few days and should show if their measurements align with the EPA's data, Billingham says.

A federal judge has blocked Trump from challenging the ABC television network's broadcast licenses. U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan ruled that the president retaliating against satire and commentary he dislikes is unconstitutional. AliKhan issued the preliminary injunction yesterday and dismissed the administration's request to throw out ABC and Disney's lawsuit challenging the review of the local license . Licenses typically last eight years and are rarely revoked. AliKhan's decision drew heavily on Trump's public statements and social media posts against ABC and Disney, as well as comments from Brendan Carr, the president's pick for chair of the Federal Communications Commission.

Holiday shopping season is in full swing. Before you spend, consider if you actually need what's in your cart. Sales are exciting because our brains are wired to seek newness. Retailers capitalize on that urge. To escape the cycle of constantly wanting more, shop intentionally and appreciate what you already own, says Eric Athas, author of Saying No to New . He shares his insights on breaking this cycle and finding joy in your current possessions with Life Kit .
🛒 Delete the app or remove your credit card info if you have one-click checkout with a company.
🛒 Add an item to your online shopping cart and leave it for 24 hours. Research shows that delaying a purchase decreases your interest in it.
🛒 Make intentional choices. Don't reject all new things. After you understand this, you can learn to say no to the wrong items and yes to the right ones.
🛒 Revisiting old things can provide you with untapped enjoyment in them, research has found. You can apply this by rereading a book or by traveling to a city you have visited before.
body_zh: 第一个简报：感恩节天气；特朗普关税；爱荷华州；美国联邦通信委员会：国家公共广播电台
第一个简报：感恩节天气；特朗普关税；爱荷华州； FCC 东海岸的天气是这个假期的主要关注点，因为它可能导致沿海洪水。而且，法官表示，联邦通信委员会不能因为特朗普不喜欢的讽刺节目而惩罚美国广播公司。
您的支持有助于我们的演出成为可能，并解锁我们的无赞助商动态。
风暴推迟了感恩节游行、特朗普的新关税、爱荷华州爆炸后
今天，席卷全国的强风暴可能会导致大范围的旅行延误，数百万人与亲人相聚。纽约市官员宣布，由于时速可能达到 60 英里的强阵风威胁，梅西百货感恩节大游行已改期至周六举行。今年是第 100 届游行，也是这一标志性活动首次被推迟。
2026 年 11 月 25 日，纽约市，工人们在 2026 年梅西百货气球充气活动期间为蜘蛛侠气球充气。梅西百货计划用创纪录的 100 个充气气球来庆祝其第 100 届感恩节游行，但预计大风可能会使巨型气球停飞。亚当·格雷/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏

NPR 的 Kat Lonsdorf 告诉 Up First，现在全国几乎每个地方都在发生一些事情。极端涨潮正在影响西海岸，中西部部分地区预计会下雪，而在南部和东南部，一场大风暴正在向东海岸推进。国家气象局天气预报中心的气象学家理查德·班恩告诉朗斯多夫，东海岸风暴是首要关注的问题。班恩表示，风暴将在全天变得更加有组织，带来强风和大雨，可能导致沿海洪水。好消息：朗斯多夫说，预报员预计东海岸的大风暴将继续下去，大部分在周六结束。
特朗普政府提议对来自中国、日本和欧盟等美国 14 个主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税。政府官员认为这些措施旨在打击不公平的外贸行为，但批评者质疑其最终效果。拟议的对中国进口商品征收的关税可能达到 40%，对越南商品征收 35%，对来自其他目标国家的产品征收 20-25%。还建议对巴西糖和飞机征收额外关税。

🎧 美国贸易大使贾米森·格里尔表示，新关税可能会在几个月内生效。 NPR 的丹妮尔·库茨莱本 (Danielle Kurtzleben) 表示，对于每个国家，白宫都列出了“提议”利率和“交易”利率。例如，如果与中国的谈判取得积极进展，他们可能会获得20%的交易率，这与提议的40%不同。尽管最高法院推翻了特朗普总统之前的关税，但新关税属于旨在打击不公平贸易行为的第 301 条法律的管辖范围。美国政府表示，这些国家在各种制成品方面表现出“结构性产能过剩”，这是由导致生产过剩的政策造成的，这可能会扭曲全球市场。
美国陆军昨天在米德尔敦的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂引爆了数千磅不稳定的叠氮化铅后，联邦科学家正在测试爱荷华州东部的空气、土壤和水的铅污染情况。官员们表示，受控爆炸是处理炸弹制造化合物的唯一安全方法。

🎧 NPR 网络电台爱荷华州公共广播电台的 Eliza Billingham 表示，主要担心的是爆炸可能导致铅释放到空气中。她补充说，自爆炸以来，美国环境保护局已经对该地区进行了测试，没有在空气中发现铅。 EPA 已部署约 300 人对空气、地面和附近的水进行采样。铅是一种神经毒素，特别危害儿童和孕妇，因为它会阻碍儿童发育。比林厄姆说，经过一周半的延误和陆军的沟通不一致，居民对陆军和环保局的初步调查结果越来越犹豫。居民希望进行独立监测，爱荷华大学和伊利诺伊大学正在进行区域抽样。比林厄姆说，预计几天后就会得出结果，并且应该显示他们的测量结果是否与美国环保局的数据相符。

一名联邦法官阻止特朗普质疑美国广播公司电视网络的广播许可证。美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗裁定，总统对他不喜欢的讽刺和评论进行报复是违宪的。阿里汗昨天发布了初步禁令，并驳回了政府的要求，即驳回美国广播公司和迪士尼对当地许可证审查提出质疑的诉讼。许可证的有效期通常为八年，很少被撤销。阿里汗的决定在很大程度上参考了特朗普针对美国广播公司和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及总统提名的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的评论。
我们的大脑天生就喜欢寻找新鲜事物，而零售业的建立就是为了让我们尽快回来购买更多东西。 J Studios/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
假日购物季正如火如荼地进行。在消费之前，请考虑您是否确实需要购物车中的商品。销售令人兴奋，因为我们的大脑天生就喜欢寻求新鲜事物。零售商利用了这种冲动。 《对新事物说不》一书的作者埃里克·阿萨斯说，为了摆脱不断想要更多的循环，有意识地购物并欣赏你已经拥有的东西。他通过 Life Kit 分享了他关于打破这个循环并在当前拥有的东西中找到快乐的见解。

title_en: Suit alleges Louisiana land deal between SpaceX and ExxonMobil violates open meetings law
title_zh: 诉讼称 SpaceX 和埃克森美孚之间的路易斯安那州土地交易违反了公开会议法
summary: Suit says parish board was manipulated to allow deal to go through and settlement agreement hidden from public After ending a lawsuit over ExxonMobil ’s damage to wetlands, Louisiana officials moved quickly to approve a deal giving SpaceX access to 125,000 acr
summary_zh: 诉讼称教区委员会被操纵，以允许交易通过，并且在结束对埃克森美孚的诉讼后向公众隐瞒和解协议
body_en: Suit alleges Louisiana land deal between SpaceX and ExxonMobil violates open meetings law | Louisiana
Suit says parish board was manipulated to allow deal to go through and settlement agreement hidden from public

After ending a lawsuit over ExxonMobil ’s damage to wetlands, Louisiana officials moved quickly to approve a deal giving SpaceX access to 125,000 acres (50,600 hectares) of marsh formerly owned by the oil company. A new lawsuit now alleges they did so in violation of the state’s open meetings law.

The lawsuit, filed by three south-central Louisiana residents, follows state and Vermilion parish officials’ approval of what is estimated to be a record $27.5bn tax incentive package for SpaceX’s Starbase Louisiana project, announced over the summer . The officials violated the state’s open meetings law eight times while facilitating the agreement in attempts to “keep the public in the dark about what they are doing for SpaceX”, the lawsuit alleges.

Prior to working on the tax abatement for SpaceX, the Vermilion parish industrial development board had not been active for nearly three decades. But in July 2026, the Vermilion parish police jury appointed seven members to the board without advance notice at the same meeting where they approved the ExxonMobil settlement, which wasn’t on the meeting agenda either, according to the lawsuit. The police jury’s legal counsel , Paul Moresi, told WWL Louisiana that the officials deny the allegations in the lawsuit and followed the requirements of the state’s open meetings law.
SpaceX plan for vast rocket launch site on Louisiana coast sparks backlash
The governor’s office then collected all copies of the settlement agreement with ExxonMobil , the details of which still remain unclear, said New Orleans attorney William Most.

“The Vermilion parish government has been violating transparency laws in totally new and unprecedented ways including using code names in public agendas and making sure they don’t keep copies of the contracts they sign so their constituents can’t read them,” Most said. “Transparency is so important because it helps prevent the state from making the same mistakes of the past and letting out-of-state corporations take our resources and hurt our citizens.”

Jackson Voss, the government affairs and policy coordinator for the Alliance for Affordable Energy , said there’s still much unknown about the deals, making it harder to know what the state is getting in return for the loss of tax revenue and potentially further damage to wetlands.

“I think that what we’ve done with this deal is subsidise both ExxonMobil and SpaceX . We’re helping two of the biggest corporations in the world to make even more money than they’re already making,” he said.
SpaceX has told locals that 30 rockets per day could be launched from the spaceport’s 10 launch pads, or about 10,000 launches per year.

Last month, a public research university in the area also entered into an agreement with SpaceX, which would allow the company to further expand the footprint of its 125,000-acre spaceport in the coastal marshlands of Vermilion parish. The University of Louisiana System Board approved the lease of five acres of UL Lafayette property to a non-profit called Ragin’ Cajun Facilities for $1 per year, as well as a sublease agreement to Space Exploration Technologies, or SpaceX.

Local residents have raised concerns about the launch site’s potential to disrupt migratory bird habitat on the cheniere surrounded by fast-eroding marshland. The lawsuit settled by ExxonMobil this summer alleged that the company was partly responsible for the severe land loss in the parish through decades of drilling activities.

Louisiana is experiencing some of the highest rates of relative sea level rise in the world, alongside alarming rates of wetland loss, estimated as a football field every 100 minutes. While the levying of the lower Mississippi River has contributed to much of the land loss in the bayou state, in Vermilion parish, wetland loss was largely caused by oil and gas activities, said coastal researcher Alex Kolker, the director of the Coastal Climates Institute.
“It’s a little different from other parts of Louisiana because you never had much of a river input,” he said. “Changes in hydrology of the Mississippi River weren’t as impactful.”

While SpaceX’s lease agreement with UL Lafayette does not say the company will launch rockets from the site, it does include a wide range of permitted uses, such as training and workforce development, warehousing and assembly, and “testing and light industrial operations”. In exchange, SpaceX agreed to invest $10m in planned improvements to the site, which was donated to the university last year for a wildlife and coastal preservation center .
Voss, with the Alliance for Affordable Energy , said that the university, as well as those responsible for the SpaceX tax deal, are making a lot of bets, without any real guarantees.

“We’re going out of our way to make sure that whatever deal is reached is the best possible for industry no matter how much it costs everyone else,” he said. “It really is like a fire sale: get what you can before it’s too late.”
body_zh: 诉讼称 SpaceX 与埃克森美孚之间的路易斯安那州土地交易违反了公开会议法路易斯安那州
诉讼称教区委员会被操纵以允许交易通过并向公众隐瞒和解协议
在结束了关于埃克森美孚破坏湿地的诉讼后，路易斯安那州官员迅速采取行动，批准了一项协议，允许 SpaceX 使用该石油公司以前拥有的 125,000 英亩（50,600 公顷）沼泽地。现在一项新的诉讼指控他们这样做违反了该州的公开会议法。
这起诉讼由路易斯安那州中南部的三名居民提起，此前州政府和弗米利恩教区官员批准了今年夏天宣布的 SpaceX 路易斯安那州 Starbase 项目估计创纪录的 275 亿美元税收激励计划。诉讼称，这些官员在促成协议达成的过程中八次违反了该州的公开会议法，试图“让公众不知道他们为 SpaceX 所做的事情”。
在为 SpaceX 减税之前，弗米利恩教区工业发展委员会已经近三十年没有活跃过。但诉讼称，2026 年 7 月，弗米利恩教区警察陪审团在批准埃克森美孚和解协议的同一次会议上，在没有提前通知的情况下任命了 7 名董事会成员，而这也没有列入会议议程。警方陪审团的法律顾问保罗·莫雷西 (Paul Moresi) 告诉 WWL 路易斯安那州官员否认诉讼中的指控，并遵守了该州公开会议法的要求。
SpaceX 计划在路易斯安那州海岸建造大型火箭发射场引发强烈反对
新奥尔良律师威廉·莫斯特表示，州长办公室随后收集了与埃克森美孚达成的和解协议的所有副本，但其细节仍不清楚。
“弗米利恩教区政府一直在以全新且前所未有的方式违反透明度法，包括在公共议程中使用代号，并确保他们不保留所签署合同的副本，以免选民无法阅读，”莫斯特说。 “透明度非常重要，因为它有助于防止国家犯过去的同样错误，防止州外公司夺走我们的资源并伤害我们的公民。”
平价能源联盟政府事务和政策协调员杰克逊·沃斯表示，这些交易仍然存在很多未知因素，因此很难知道该州因税收损失和湿地可能进一步受损而得到的回报。
“我认为我们通过这笔交易所做的是补贴埃克森美孚和 SpaceX。我们正在帮助世界上最大的两家公司赚取比他们已经赚到的更多的钱，”他说。
SpaceX 告诉当地人，该航天港的 10 个发射台每天可以发射 30 枚火箭，或者每年大约发射 10,000 次。

上个月，该地区的一所公立研究大学也与 SpaceX 签订了一项协议，该协议将使该公司能够进一步扩大其位于弗米利恩教区沿海沼泽地、占地 125,000 英亩的太空港的占地面积。路易斯安那大学系统委员会批准以每年 1 美元的价格向名为 Ragin’ Cajun Facilities 的非营利组织租赁 UL Lafayette 的 5 英亩土地，并签署了向太空探索技术公司 (SpaceX) 的转租协议。
当地居民担心发射场可能会破坏切尼尔周围的候鸟栖息地，周围是快速侵蚀的沼泽地。埃克森美孚今年夏天和解的诉讼称，该公司对数十年钻探活动导致该教区土地严重流失负有部分责任。
路易斯安那州正经历着世界上相对海平面上升速度最快的时期，同时湿地的损失速度也惊人，估计每 100 分钟就有一个足球场那么大。沿海气候研究所所长、沿海研究员亚历克斯·科尔克表示，虽然密西西比河下游的征税造成了河口州大部分土地流失，但在弗米利恩教区，湿地流失主要是由石油和天然气活动造成的。
“这与路易斯安那州的其他地区有点不同，因为这里从来没有太多的河流输入，”他说。 “密西西比河水文的变化没有那么有影响力。”
虽然 SpaceX 与 UL Lafayette 的租赁协议并未规定该公司将从该场地发射火箭，但它确实包括了广泛的许可用途，例如培训和劳动力发展、仓储和组装以及“测试和轻工业运营”。作为交换，SpaceX 同意投资 1000 万美元用于计划中的场地改进，该场地去年已捐赠给该大学，用于建设野生动物和海岸保护中心。
平价能源联盟的沃斯表示，该大学以及负责 SpaceX 税收协议的人正在进行大量押注，但没有任何真正的保证。
他说：“我们将竭尽全力确保达成的任何协议都是对行业来说最好的，无论其他各方付出多少代价。” “这真的就像一次甩卖：在为时已晚之前尽你所能。”

title_en: Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
title_zh: 参议院民主党团体推动增加新人担任领导层
summary: Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.
summary_zh: 几位民主党参议员一直在暗示这一举措，称该党需要承认即将入学的新生的多元化阶层
body_en: Group of Senate Democrats Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.

U.S. Senate Majority Leader Charles Schumer (D-NY), center, is seen here meeting with newly elected Democratic Senators, (L-R) Senator-elect Andy Kim (D-NJ), Senator-elect Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Senator-elect Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) Senator-elect Adam Schiff (D-CA) Senator-elect Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Senator-elect Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) at the U.S. Capitol Building on November 12, 2024. That group of senators is pushing to add an incoming freshman senator to the leadership ranks. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/Getty Images North America hide caption
A group of Senate Democrats elected in 2024 sent a letter to colleagues Tuesday proposing to add an incoming freshman to the leadership ranks.

"The Freshman Representative to Leadership would be elected by members of the incoming freshman class and confirmed by the Conference," the letter said. "We intend to request a vote on this proposal."

The letter, first reported by Politico , is signed by California Sen. Adam Schiff, Maryland Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, Delaware Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, and New Jersey Sen. Andy Kim.
The letter nods to the diverse class of incoming freshmen who helped catapult the party to controlling both chambers of Congress.

"These freshmen have their fingers on the pulse of long-time Democratic voters, those who voted for Democrats for the first time this past Election Day, and everyone in-between," the letter reads. "The deserve a seat at the table."
Senate Democrats have been signaling a desire to uplift new voices in the party.
"On election night, people voted very clearly for a new generation of leadership. That was very, very clear," Slotkin said during remarks at a conference of Democrats after the midterms .
New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker told MS NOW that leadership extends beyond the top post.

"This is a time for new leadership," Booker said, mentioning wanting to see more of incoming Sens. Annie Andrews of South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas. "I want to see them out front, I want to see them taking issues, I want to see them running on the field."
The proposed rule change comes ahead of the leadership election next week. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., for the majority leader.

Senate leadership is comprised not only of the top position of Majority leader but of additional conference officers. Both Van Hollen and Schumer support the idea of adding a position for a freshman to that leadership group.
"Leader Schumer was already planning to do this and is incredibly supportive of the idea," a spokesperson told NPR.

On Tuesday, Van Hollen posted to social media: "There should be a freshman senator on the Senate leadership team. As I've said, we need a new way to organize so we can deliver for the American people."

body_zh: 参议院民主党团体 几位民主党参议员已经发出了这一举动的信号，称该党需要承认不同阶层的新生，正是他们使该党在 11 月取得了胜利。

美国参议院多数党领袖查尔斯·舒默（纽约州民主党）（中）与新当选的民主党参议员会面，从左到右当选参议员安迪·金（新泽西州民主党）、当选参议员鲁本·加列戈（亚利桑那州民主党）、当选参议员安吉拉·阿尔斯布鲁克斯（马里兰州民主党）、当选参议员亚当·希夫（加利福尼亚州民主党）、当选参议员丽莎·布伦特·罗切斯特（德国民主党）和当选参议员2024 年 11 月 12 日，埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (密歇根州民主党议员) 在美国国会大厦。这群参议员正在推动将一位即将上任的新参议员加入领导层。奇普·索莫德维拉/盖蒂图片社/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
一群 2024 年当选的参议院民主党人周二致信同事，提议在领导层中增加一名即将上任的新人。
信中说：“新生领导层代表将由新生班成员选举产生，并由大会确认。” “我们打算要求对该提案进行投票。”
这封信最先由 Politico 报道，由加利福尼亚州参议员 Adam Schiff、马里兰州参议员 Angela Alsobrooks、密歇根州参议员 Elissa Slotkin、亚利桑那州参议员 Ruben Gallego、特拉华州参议员 Lisa Blunt Rochester 和新泽西州参议员 Andy Kim 签署。
这封信向不同阶层的新生致敬，他们帮助该党控制了国会两院。
信中写道：“这些新生掌握着长期民主党选民的脉搏，那些在过去的选举日首次投票给民主党的人，以及中间的每个人。” “他们应该在谈判桌上占有一席之地。”
参议院民主党人一直表示希望在党内发出新的声音。
“在选举之夜，人们非常明确地投票支持新一代领导层。这是非常非常明确的，”斯洛特金在中期选举后的民主党会议上发表讲话时表示。
新泽西州参议员科里·布克 (Cory Booker) 告诉《MS NOW》，领导力不仅仅局限于最高职位。
布克说：“这是新领导层的时刻。”他提到希望看到更多即将上任的南卡罗来纳州参议员安妮·安德鲁斯和德克萨斯州参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科。 “我想看到他们在前面，我想看到他们解决问题，我想看到他们在球场上奔跑。”
拟议的规则变更是在下周的领导人选举之前提出的。马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 正在挑战参议院少数党领袖、纽约州民主党人查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 的多数党领袖席位。
参议院的领导层不仅由多数党领袖的最高职位组成，还由其他会议官员组成。范霍伦和舒默都支持在该领导小组中增加一个新人职位的想法。
“领导人舒默已经计划这样做，并且非常支持这个想法，”一位发言人告诉 NPR。
周二，范霍伦在社交媒体上发帖称：“参议院领导团队中应该有一名新参议员。正如我所说，我们需要一种新的组织方式，以便我们能够为美国人民做出贡献。”

title_en: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
title_zh: 共和党人希望联邦调查局和中央情报局在质询英伟达首席执行官之前得到答案
summary: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.
summary_zh: 这位共和党议员表示：“公众的担忧是正确的。”他想知道联邦调查局和中央情报局对潜在的国家安全威胁了解多少
body_en: GOP lawmaker seeks answers over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang : NPR

GOP lawmaker seeks answers over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Penn., on Nvidia CEO's upcoming House committee interview
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., speaks at a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing in Washington on Sept. 21, 2022. Samuel Corum/Getty Images hide caption
Lawmakers seek answers on the national security as Nvidia CEO returns
Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia with President Trump's backing. But the questions surrounding the AI chipmaker and its ties to China are far from settled.

U.S. intelligence officials told congressional staff there is no evidence that Alice Huang, the woman who had an affair with the Nvidia chief, was a Chinese spy or intelligence asset, according to a person familiar with the matter who was granted anonymity to speak about a closed-door briefing.

There is also no evidence that she initiated the affair to collect intelligence for China's government, the person told NPR's Ryan Lucas on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the matter. She is, however, believed to have passed along information after the affair began.

Trump has said he helped arrange Huang's return as CEO, and Nvidia's board maintains that his reinstatement presents no national security risk. Some Republican lawmakers, however, want to understand how those conclusions were reached.

Speaking to Morning Edition on Wednesday, before NPR obtained the new information, Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., said he wants to hear from the FBI and CIA before Huang appears before House lawmakers next week.

For Fitzpatrick, a former FBI special agent who sits on the House Intelligence Committee, the inquiry begins with what federal authorities knew and whether they warned the Nvidia chief of potential espionage threats.
"What briefings did they give? When did they give them?" he asked.
Huang's reinstatement, Fitzpatrick said, should not put those questions to rest.
"The public is rightly concerned, and they deserve answers," he said.

Fitzpatrick also wants to hear from Attorney General Todd Blanche, who on Tuesday described Nvidia as a good corporate citizen, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department faces questions over Nvidia's chip exports to China.
"Anytime you do an investigation, you follow the facts wherever they lead, and you report those facts with unimpeachable integrity," Fitzpatrick said. "You leave no stone unturned."
The debate over Huang's reinstatement extends beyond Washington.
In Silicon Valley, his return has alarmed women and advocates who have spent years pushing for a better workplace culture, renewing questions about the limits of executive accountability.

body_zh: 共和党议员寻求英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的答案：NPR
共和党议员寻求英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的答案 这位共和党议员表示，“公众的担忧是正确的”，他想知道联邦调查局和中央情报局对潜在的国家安全威胁了解多少，以及黄仁勋是否受到警告。
宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 接受 Nvidia 首席执行官即将接受的众议院委员会采访
宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 于 2022 年 9 月 21 日在华盛顿举行的众议院外交事务小组委员会听证会上发表讲话。塞缪尔·科鲁姆/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
英伟达首席执行官回归后，立法者寻求国家安全问题的答案
在特朗普总统的支持下，黄仁勋重新执掌英伟达。但围绕这家人工智能芯片制造商及其与中国的关系的问题还远未解决。
据一位不愿透露姓名的知情人士透露，美国情报官员告诉国会工作人员，没有证据表明与英伟达首席执行官有染的女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是中国间谍或情报人员。
该人士对美国国家公共广播电台的瑞安·卢卡斯表示，也没有证据表明她发起了这起事件是为了为中国政府收集情报。由于此事敏感，该人士要求匿名。然而，据信她在事件开始后就传递了信息。
特朗普表示，他帮助安排了黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，而英伟达董事会坚称，他的复职不会带来国家安全风险。然而，一些共和党议员想了解这些结论是如何得出的。
周三，在 NPR 获得新信息之前，宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 表示，他希望在黄下周出现在众议院议员面前之前听取联邦调查局 (FBI) 和中央情报局 (CIA) 的意见。
对于担任众议院情报委员会成员的前联邦调查局特工菲茨帕特里克来说，调查始于联邦当局所知道的情况以及他们是否警告过英伟达负责人潜在的间谍威胁。
“他们做了什么简报？他们什么时候做的？”他问道。
菲茨帕特里克说，黄的复职不应消除这些问题。
“公众的担忧是正确的，他们应该得到答案，”他说。
菲茨帕特里克还希望听取司法部长托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克（Howard Lutnick）的意见，前者周二将英伟达描述为良好的企业公民，后者的部门面临英伟达向中国出口芯片的质疑。
菲茨帕特里克说：“无论何时进行调查，你都会遵循事实，无论事实如何，并以无可挑剔的诚信报告这些事实。” “你不遗余力。”
关于黄的复职的争论超出了华盛顿范围。
在硅谷，他的回归引起了女性和倡导者的警惕，她们多年来一直在推动更好的工作场所文化，并重新提出了关于高管问责制局限性的问题。

title_en: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
title_zh: 特朗普在敦促黄仁勋复职时拥有数百万英伟达股票
summary: President Trump holds tens of millions in Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride of the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统持有数千万英伟达股票，这让他个人在过去两年该公司股市的过山车之旅中占有一席之地
body_en: President Trump holds tens of millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride over the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.

Mr. Trump stood to lose large sums with CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure, and stood to profit handsomely after he successfully pressed the chip developer's board to reinstate Huang. Nvidia stock surged more than 30% when Huang returned to the company on Monday, reversing a weekslong slide.

Huang resigned two weeks ago over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who ran a company accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China, and another alleged affair with a subordinate. Mr. Trump said Monday he personally spoke with Nvidia's board and "convinced them" to rehire Huang, offering an "assurance" that there was no national security threat.

Mr. Trump held between $13 million and $58 million in Nvidia stock in his investment accounts as of the end of 2025, according to financial disclosures filed with the Office of Government Ethics. He bought or sold the company's stock in more than 100 transactions that were worth between $27 million and nearly $98 million between January 2025 and September 2026.

The value of the president's Nvidia shares increased anywhere from $1.3 million to $14.8 million on Monday, before paring back some of those gains when Nvidia's share price ticked down Tuesday. The range is so large because it isn't clear how many shares of Nvidia the president currently owns, but it can be roughly estimated based on his sales and purchases this year.

"President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions," a White House spokesman told CBS News Tuesday, adding that his investments mirror indexes like the Schwab 1000. "Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers."

In addition to the president, several of his appointees to positions in the State, Commerce and Treasury departments as well as the IRS reported millions in Nvidia stock in their investment portfolios. Many have since sold their holdings.

Forbes estimates Mr. Trump's net worth at more than $6 billion, making Nvidia a small part of his total wealth. And Nvidia is one of the world's most valuable public companies, at more than $3.7 trillion, so many investors hold shares in the tech giant.
Still, some ethics experts questioned Mr. Trump's large stake in Nvidia, especially after he intervened to boost the company's fortunes.

"This goes beyond a conflict of interest," said Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "He is squarely, explicitly using his power as president to benefit himself financially. He has prioritized his finances over the security of the nation."

Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit government watchdog, told CBS News that Mr. Trump's "continued ownership of stock in this company is the clearest example of how the president's personal financial interest makes everything he does suspect."

Mr. Trump's personal investments have drawn controversy in the past, including his stakes in publicly traded energy companies, firms that have business with the government and his family's cryptocurrency firm . He has denied any conflict of interest.

Some critics called for legal reforms to prohibit the president and members of Congress from buying and selling stocks while they hold office. Elected officials are generally allowed to trade individual stocks, though lawmakers from both parties have called for the practice to be banned.

Richard Painter, a law professor at the University of Minnesota and former chief ethics attorney for the White House between 2005 and 2007, said he has long argued for changes to the federal conflict of interest law that prohibits government employees from participating in matters that result in their personal enrichment while in office. That current law does not apply to the president, vice president or members of Congress, he said.
"We need a prohibition on this right away," he said, adding that the new Congress may take up the cause in January.
Painter called Mr. Trump's intervention with the Nvidia board "a huge conflict of interest" and overreach of government power.
"It's not the job of the government to call up and say who the CEO of a company should be," he told CBS News.

The president has defended his decision to intervene , saying on CNBC that "we have to protect our geniuses" and arguing that Nvidia — as the world's leading designer of advanced chips — plays a key role in maintaining the U.S.' lead over China in AI technology.

Mr. Trump has also frequently pointed to the performance of the stock market as a barometer of his success as president. Shortly after Huang was reinstated, Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal the "response from the market has been very positive," and "that really shows the decision was right."
Beyond Mr. Trump, numerous political appointees held Nvidia stock. Some divested themselves of their holdings after they were appointed to government positions, federal filings show.
body_zh: 财务披露文件显示，特朗普总统持有价值数千万美元的英伟达股票，这让他在过去两周该公司股市的过山车之旅中占有一席之地。
由于首席执行官黄仁勋的突然离职，特朗普可能会损失巨额资金，但在他成功迫使芯片开发商董事会恢复黄仁勋的职位后，他将获得丰厚的利润。当黄周一重返公司时，英伟达股价飙升超过 30%，扭转了长达一周的下滑局面。
两周前，黄仁勋因涉嫌与一名中国间谍有染而辞职，该间谍经营一家被指控将英伟达芯片转移到中国的公司，以及另一起涉嫌与一名下属发生婚外情的报道。特朗普周一表示，他亲自与英伟达董事会进行了交谈，并“说服他们”重新雇用黄仁勋，并“保证”不存在国家安全威胁。
根据政府道德办公室提交的财务披露信息，截至 2025 年底，特朗普的投资账户中持有价值 1,300 万至 5,800 万美元的 Nvidia 股票。 2025 年 1 月至 2026 年 9 月期间，他通过 100 多笔交易购买或出售了该公司的股票，价值在 2700 万美元至近 9800 万美元之间。
周一，总统持有的 Nvidia 股票价值从 130 万美元增至 1,480 万美元，周二 Nvidia 股价下跌，部分涨幅回吐。这个范围之所以如此之大，是因为目前尚不清楚总裁目前拥有多少英伟达股票，但可以根据他今年的销售和购买情况粗略​​估计。
白宫发言人周二告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，“特朗普总统的股票和债券投资组合由第三方金融机构独立管理。”他补充说，他的投资反映了嘉信1000等指数。“特朗普总统和他的任何家庭成员都没有能力指导、影响或提供有关投资组合投资方式或何时购买或出售投资的意见。所有投资决策完全由独立管理者做出。”
除了总统之外，他任命的几位在国务院、商务部、财政部以及国税局任职的人都报告说，他们的投资组合中持有数百万美元的英伟达股票。此后许多人出售了所持股份。
《福布斯》估计特朗普的净资产超过 60 亿美元，英伟达只占他总财富的一小部分。英伟达是世界上最有价值的上市公司之一，价值超过 3.7 万亿美元，因此许多投资者持有这家科技巨头的股票。
尽管如此，一些道德专家仍对特朗普在英伟达持有的大量股份提出质疑，尤其是在他介入以提振该公司的财富之后。
“这超出了利益冲突的范畴，”圣路易斯华盛顿大学法学教授兼政府道德专家凯瑟琳·克拉克 (Kathleen Clark) 说。 “他直接、明确地利用总统的权力为自己谋取经济利益。他将自己的财务置于国家安全之上。”
华盛顿非营利性政府监管机构公民责任与道德组织主席唐纳德·谢尔曼告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，特朗普“继续持有这家公司的股票是最明显的例子，说明总统的个人经济利益如何让他所做的一切都受到怀疑。”
特朗普的个人投资过去曾引起争议，包括他在上市能源公司、与政府有业务往来的公司以及其家族的加密货币公司中的股份。他否认有任何利益冲突。
一些批评者呼吁进行法律改革，禁止总统和国会议员在任职期间买卖股票。民选官员通常可以交易个股，但两党议员都呼吁禁止这种做法。
明尼苏达大学法学教授、2005年至2007年任白宫首席道德律师理查德·佩因特(Richard Painter)表示，他长期以来一直主张修改联邦利益冲突法，该法禁止政府雇员在任职期间参与导致个人致富的事务。他说，现行法律不适用于总统、副总统或国会议员。
他说：“我们需要立即禁止这一行为。”他补充说，新国会可能会在一月份着手解决这一问题。
佩因特称特朗普对英伟达董事会的干预是“巨大的利益冲突”以及政府权力的越权。
他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻：“政府的职责不是召集并规定谁应该担任公司首席执行官。”
总统为自己的干预决定进行了辩护，他在 CNBC 上表示，“我们必须保护我们的天才”，并认为英伟达作为全球领先的先进芯片设计商，在维持美国地位方面发挥着关键作用。人工智能技术领先中国。
特朗普还经常指出股市表现是他作为总统成功与否的晴雨表。黄仁勋复职后不久，特朗普对《华尔街日报》表示，“市场的反应非常积极”，“这确实表明这个决定是正确的”。
除了特朗普之外，许多政治任命者也持有英伟达股票。联邦文件显示，一些人在被任命担任政府职位后剥离了自己的股份。

title_en: FedEx cargo plane runs off MIA runway, causing brief ground stop
title_zh: 联邦快递货机冲出迈阿密国际机场跑道，造成短暂地面停留
summary: The Miami-Dade Fire-Rescue and Sheriff's Office both confirmed that two people were on board the plane and no injuries were reported.
summary_zh: 迈阿密戴德消防局和治安官办公室均证实飞机上有两人，没有人员受伤的报告。
body_en: FedEx cargo plane runs off Miami International Airport runway, causing ground stop during Thanksgiving travel - CBS News
A FedEx cargo plane ran off a runway at Miami International Airport amid wind and rain Wednesday night, prompting a temporary ground stop during one of the busiest travel days of the year.

According to an FAA advisory, departures bound for Miami were grounded until at least 9:45 p.m. Preliminary reports indicate a FedEx McDonnell Douglas MD-11 cargo plane went off the runway, prompting the halt in incoming air traffic.
The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said it responded to the runway at MIA at approximately 8:40 p.m. and found the cargo plane.
Neither of the two people on board was injured, and responding emergency crews from both the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue reported no signs of fire or smoke.
MIA posted on X, confirming the incident happened at Runway 26R and that all runways were closed except for Runway 9R.

A FedEx aircraft overran Runway 26R at Miami International Airport at approximately 8:40 p.m. All runways are closed except for runway 9R. @MiamiDadeFire units have responded, and there are no reported injuries. Passengers scheduled to travel tonight are encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight updates before heading to the airport. We appreciate our passengers' patience as we work to safely resume normal operations.
Miami Int'l Airport (@iflymia) https://x.com/iflymia/status/2125777705194963111?ref_src=twsrc^tfw Edit Unlink ' rel="noopener">November 26, 2026

Minutes before flights were set to resume, the FAA also posted on X about the incident, confirming that the FedEx McDonnell Douglas MD-11 had departed from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis.
Wet weather investigated as a possible cause for the incident
At the time of the incident, rainy conditions had reduced visibility to 7 miles, with a 13-mph tailwind reported at the airfield.
An airport employee who witnessed the aftermath and asked not to be named said the crew appeared to struggle to slow the aircraft on the wet pavement before it veered onto the grass.

"They tried as hard as they could to stop, but I don't know if it was the weather because the rain and the wind were really bad, and they just couldn't stop in time and went right off the runway and veered off into the grass," the employee said.
The worker noted that the overrun occurred on the airport's shortest runway, raising renewed concerns following a September Amazon cargo plane crash that killed five people.
The brief ground stop Wednesday left some Thanksgiving travelers waiting for hours before flight operations resumed.

"I'm kind of shocked," traveler Dennis Pastorizo said. "I didn't think that a delivery plane would cause a two-hour delay for a flight to the other side of the country, especially on one of the busiest [travel days] of the year."
FedEx issued a statement to CBS News Miami about the incident that says

"FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport. We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA."
The FAA announced Wednesday night that it is investigating the incident.

周三晚上，一架联邦快递货机在风雨中冲出迈阿密国际机场跑道，导致在一年中最繁忙的旅行日之一期间暂时停飞。
根据美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 的建议，飞往迈阿密的航班至少要停飞到晚上 9:45。初步报告显示，一架联邦快递麦道 MD-11 货机冲出跑道，导致来港空中交通中断。
迈阿密-戴德县治安官办公室表示，他们于晚上 8 点 40 分左右对迈阿密国际机场的跑道做出了回应。并找到了货机。
机上两人均未受伤，迈阿密戴德警长办公室和迈阿密戴德消防救援队的应急人员均报告没有火灾或烟雾迹象。
迈阿密国际机场在 X 上发帖，确认事件发生在 26R 跑道，并且除 9R 跑道外，所有跑道均已关闭。
晚上 8 点 40 分左右，一架联邦快递飞机冲出了迈阿密国际机场 26R 跑道。除 9R 跑道外，所有跑道均已关闭。 @MiamiDadeFire 单位已做出回应，目前尚无人员伤亡报告。我们鼓励计划今晚出行的乘客在前往机场之前直接向航空公司查询最新航班信息。我们感谢乘客在我们努力安全恢复正常运营过程中的耐心等待。
迈阿密国际机场 (@iflymia) https://x.com/iflymia/status/2125777705194963111?ref_src=twsrc^tfw 编辑取消链接 ' rel="noopener">2026 年 11 月 26 日
在航班恢复前几分钟，美国联邦航空局还在 X 上发布了有关该事件的信息，确认联邦快递麦道 MD-11 已从孟菲斯弗雷德里克·W·史密斯国际机场起飞。
潮湿天气被调查为事故的可能原因
事件发生时，多雨天气使能见度降至 7 英里，据报道机场顺风速度为 13 英里/小时。
一位目睹了整个过程并要求匿名的机场工作人员表示，在飞机转向草地之前，机组人员似乎很难在潮湿的路面上放慢飞机速度。
“他们竭尽全力想停下来，但我不知道是不是天气原因，因为雨和风都很大，他们就是没能及时停下来，直接冲出了跑道，冲进了草地，”这名员工说。
这名工作人员指出，超跑道发生在机场最短的跑道上，继 9 月份亚马逊货机坠毁导致 5 人死亡后，这再次引发了人们的担忧。
周三的短暂地面停留让一些感恩节旅客在航班恢复运营前等待了几个小时。
“我有点震惊，”旅行者丹尼斯·帕斯托里佐说。 “我不认为运送飞机会导致飞往该国另一边的航班延误两个小时，尤其是在一年中最繁忙的[旅行日]之一。”
联邦快递就这一事件向哥伦比亚广播公司迈阿密新闻发表了一份声明，称
“从孟菲斯飞往迈阿密的联邦快递 910 航班周三晚上在迈阿密国际机场降落时遇到了问题。我们很高兴我们的机组人员很安全，并且没有受伤的报告。我们正在与调查当局密切合作，任何其他问题应提交给美国联邦航空局。”
美国联邦航空局周三晚间宣布正在调查这一事件。

title_en: Oil prices inch back up as Iran and the Houthis escalate threats
title_zh: 随着伊朗和胡塞武装威胁升级，油价小幅回升
summary: Increased fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia and Tehran's unrelenting threats in the Strait of Hormuz appear to be reversing weeks of oil price declines.
summary_zh: 伊朗胡塞盟友与沙特阿拉伯之间的战斗加剧，以及德黑兰在霍尔木兹海峡的无情威胁似乎正在扭转数周的局面
body_en: Global oil prices, which had dropped about 20% in recent weeks with the U.S.-Iran war locked in a stalemate, have risen again slightly as Tehran threatens to increase attacks on ships and fighting between its Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia escalates.

Ship transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen again this month and the amount of oil and other products being shipped out of the Persian Gulf remains at just over half of pre-war levels, according to shipping intelligence firm Kpler.
The Iran-backed Houthi group claimed an attack on the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital on Wednesday, as well on a sprawling oil refinery in the country's east.
33m ago Body of Jordanian sailor found off UAE coast after vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz

The body of a Jordanian sailor who was reported missing after an Iranian attack on his vessel in the Strait of Hormuz last week, was found off the coast of Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates, Jordan's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday .
"The body of Mohamed Hossam al-Din al-Otaibi , may he rest in peace, was found on Wednesday," the ministry said.

The United Arab Emirates' state-owned ADNOC energy company reported the sailor missing last week after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. It said 11 crew members were injured in the attack.
The Jordanian ministry praised the efforts of UAE and Omani authorities for locating the sailor's body.

5:38 AM Iran claims 2 more tankers ablaze after hitting sea mines in Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Thursday that two "non-compliant" oil tankers were on fire after striking sea mines while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz via southern shipping lanes the U.S. military insists are safe, but Tehran has repeatedly warned vessels to avoid.

"Since the early hours of today, two non-compliant oil tankers have exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines north of the port of Khasab," which is on the Omani coast in the center of the strait, Iranian state media quoted the IRGC as saying.

The report, which was not immediately corroborated by independent maritime agencies, said one of the ships was a supertanker laden with more than 2 million barrels of crude oil that was left burning after hitting a mine.

The statement — the latest in a series of daily claims by the Iranian regime of ships striking mines in the strait — came after IRGC Navy commander Rear Adm. Ali Azmaei reiterated Tehran's warning to shipping firms that passage through the strait would only be safe "by respecting Iran's sovereignty."

"We not only have control of this waterway, but have also placed the power to change the equations at the heart of the Strait of Hormuz," declared Azmaei, whose remarks were also carried by state media.

5:13 AM Ship traffic through Strait of Hormuz has dropped significantly this month, maritime intel firm says

Ship transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen again this month and the amount of crude oil and other products shipped outside the Persian Gulf remains at just over half of pre-war levels, according to data from shipping intelligence company Kpler.
The number of ships making the journey per week fell from 217 to 147 between Nov. 1 and Nov. 23, Kpler said in two reports this week.

Tanker crossings averaged 11 per day for the week ending Nov. 21, compared to 50 per day before the war, meanwhile, though the company noted that many crossings are "dark," or done with their AIS transmission systems turned off, usually for safety reasons.
body_zh: 最近几周，随着美伊战争陷入僵局，全球油价已下跌约 20%，但随着德黑兰威胁增加对船只的袭击以及其胡塞盟友与沙特阿拉伯之间的战斗升级，全球油价再次小幅上涨。
据航运情报公司 Kpler 称，本月通过霍尔木兹海峡的船舶运输量再次下降，从波斯湾运出的石油和其他产品的数量仍仅略高于战前水平的一半。
伊朗支持的胡塞武装声称周三对沙特阿拉伯首都金融区以及该国东部一座庞大的炼油厂发动了袭击。
33m 前 霍尔木兹海峡船只遇袭，约旦水手尸体在阿联酋海岸被发现
约旦外交部周四表示，一名约旦水手的尸体在阿拉伯联合酋长国哈伊马角海岸被发现，该水手上周在霍尔木兹海峡遭到伊朗袭击，据报道失踪。
该部表示：“穆罕默德·霍萨姆·丁·奥泰比的尸体于周三被发现，愿他安息。”
阿拉伯联合酋长国国有的ADNOC能源公司报告称，上周该公司的一艘船只在霍尔木兹海峡遭到袭击后，这名水手失踪。据称，11名船员在袭击中受伤。
约旦外交部赞扬阿联酋和阿曼当局为找到该水手尸体所做的努力。
凌晨 5:38 伊朗声称另外 2 艘油轮在霍尔木兹海峡触雷后起火
伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队周四声称，两艘“不合规”油轮在试图通过美国军方坚称安全的南部航道穿越霍尔木兹海峡时触雷后起火，但德黑兰一再警告船只避开。
伊朗官方媒体援引伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队的消息称，“从今天凌晨开始，两艘不合规的油轮在袭击位于海峡中心阿曼海岸的海塞卜港以北的水雷后发生爆炸并起火。”
该报道称，其中一艘船是一艘载有超过 200 万桶原油的超级油轮，该油轮在触雷后燃烧，该报告并未立即得到独立海事机构的证实。
伊朗革命卫队海军司令阿里·阿兹迈伊少将重申了德黑兰对航运公司的警告，只有“尊重伊朗主权”，通过该海峡才能安全。
阿兹迈伊宣称：“我们不仅控制了这条水道，而且还拥有改变霍尔木兹海峡中心方程式的力量。”他的言论也被官方媒体转载。
凌晨 5:13 海事情报公司表示，本月通过霍尔木兹海峡的船舶交通量大幅下降
航运情报公司 Kpler 的数据显示，本月通过霍尔木兹海峡的船舶运输量再次下降，波斯湾以外地区的原油和其他产品运输量仍仅略高于战前水平的一半。
Kpler 在本周的两份报告中表示，11 月 1 日至 23 日期间，每周航行的船舶数量从 217 艘下降到 147 艘。
截至 11 月 21 日的一周，油轮过境点平均每天有 11 趟，而战前每天有 50 趟，不过该公司指出，许多过境点是“黑暗的”，或者是在关闭 AIS 传输系统的情况下进行的，通常是出于安全原因。
